# @saigontechnology/vision-camera-background-filter

> Real-time selfie background replacement for react-native-vision-camera 5, plus a
> record-time capture that puts the background into the delivered file and an offline
> bake as fallback. Segmentation and compositing are native (iOS Vision / Android MLKit);
> no mask crosses into JS.
> Full reference: ./llms-full.txt
> Human docs: ./README.md

React Native >=0.78 (New Architecture), React >=19, iOS 15+ to segment, Android minSdk 24
/ compileSdk 36. **Does not run in Expo Go** — needs a dev build.

## Install

```bash
npx expo install @saigontechnology/vision-camera-background-filter \
  react-native-vision-camera react-native-vision-camera-worklets \
  react-native-nitro-modules react-native-nitro-image react-native-worklets
npx expo install expo-file-system expo-camera   # optional, recommended
```

1. `babel.config.js` → add `'react-native-worklets/plugin'` as the LAST plugin.
2. Permissions come from `expo-camera`'s config plugin (`cameraPermission`,
   `microphonePermission`, `recordAudioAndroid: true`). This package ships NO config
   plugin. Do not also write the Info.plist keys by hand — that yields conflicting keys.
3. `expo-build-properties` → `compileSdkVersion: 36`, `minSdkVersion: 24`,
   iOS `deploymentTarget: '15.1'`.
4. `npx expo prebuild --clean && npx expo run:ios`.
5. Bare RN: `yarn add` the same peers, `pod install`, set `minSdkVersion`/
   `compileSdkVersion` in `android/build.gradle`, add CAMERA + RECORD_AUDIO permissions.

Verify the native side linked before writing UI:
`getSegmentationSupport()` must return `{ supported: true }`. If it does not on a capable
device, the module did not link — rebuild, do not debug JS.

## Configure the host (once, at startup)

The package does not choose a filesystem library. Supply two members before any camera
screen mounts.

```ts
import { configureBackgroundFilterHost } from '@saigontechnology/vision-camera-background-filter';
import { createExpoBackgroundFilterHost } from '@saigontechnology/vision-camera-background-filter/adapters/expo';

configureBackgroundFilterHost(createExpoBackgroundFilterHost());
```

Non-Expo: `configureBackgroundFilterHost({ fileSystem: { cacheDirectory, deleteFile }, onWarn })`.
`cacheDirectory` is a PLAIN PATH with a trailing slash and NO `file://` scheme — Android's
MediaMuxer rejects a URI. Skipping this is safe: the capture is skipped and the offline
bake takes over.

## Canonical usage

```tsx
import {
  BACKGROUND_NONE,
  DEFAULT_BACKGROUNDS,
  isBackgroundFilterAvailable,
  VisionCameraSurface,
  type CameraSurfaceHandle,
} from '@saigontechnology/vision-camera-background-filter';
import { ExpoCameraSurface } from '@saigontechnology/vision-camera-background-filter/surfaces/expo-camera';

const ref = useRef<CameraSurfaceHandle>(null);
const [backgroundId, setBackgroundId] = useState(BACKGROUND_NONE);

// ONCE per mount — never on every render.
const [available] = useState(() => isBackgroundFilterAvailable());
const Surface = available ? VisionCameraSurface : ExpoCameraSurface;

<Surface
  ref={ref}
  style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill}
  facing="front"
  onReady={() => setReady(true)}
  backgroundId={backgroundId}
  backgrounds={MY_BACKGROUNDS} // optional; REPLACES the bundled defaults
/>;

const result = await ref.current?.record(30); // resolves when recording stops
if (result == null) return;                   // session torn down — NOT an error
if (result.hasBackground) upload(result.uri); // background already in the pixels
else upload(await bakeIfNeeded(result.uri, backgroundId));
```

Fallback bake for a clip that came back without its background:

```tsx
if (shouldBakeBackground({ background: backgroundId })) {
  const { outputPath } = await processVideoBackground({
    inputPath: trimmedUri,
    background: findBackground(MY_BACKGROUNDS, backgroundId)!,
    fit: 'cover',
    mirror: false,
    onProgress: (p) => setPct(Math.round(p * 100)),
    signal: controller.signal,
  });
}
```

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

1. Branch on `result.hasBackground`, NEVER on the user's selected background. A capture
   that failed reports `false` even though a background was picked; that is what makes
   the fallback safe. Branching on the selection uploads clips missing their background.
2. `record()` resolving `undefined` means the session was torn down (user navigated away)
   — not a failure. Only a rejection is. On iOS a teardown REJECTS, so check an
   `unmounted` ref before showing an error.
3. Resolve the surface component ONCE per mount (`useState(() => …)`). Swapping
   mid-session tears down a live capture session.
4. Do NOT wrap the optional deps in `try { require() }`. Metro resolves `require`
   statically, so an uninstalled package is a BUILD error and the catch never runs.
   Optionality comes from the subpath exports — import them or do not.
5. Hide the background picker when `isBackgroundFilterAvailable()` is false.
6. Trim before you bake. The bake runs 0.3–1x realtime (10–60 s for 30 s) and needs a
   progress UI and a cancel path.
7. A failed bake must ABORT the submit, not upload silently — that reads as data loss.
   `isCancelledBakeError(e)` distinguishes a user cancel from a real failure.
8. The background is never mirrored on either path. Set `mirrorCamera: facing === 'front'`,
   leave `mirror: false`.
9. Reset the background to `none` on flip to the rear camera — both models are tuned for
   front-facing selfies.
10. React Native overlays (teleprompter, countdown, watermark) are NOT composited into
    the file. That is correct and intentional.
11. `CameraRecording.uri` is a SCHEMELESS absolute path on Android (not `file://`).
    ExoPlayer plays it fine, but `expo-video`'s `generateThumbnailsAsync` checks
    `URLUtil.isFileUrl` (literally `startsWith("file:")`), fails, and falls through to
    the NETWORK overload of `setDataSource` — the video plays and the thumbnail strip is
    empty, on Android only. Prefix `file://` for the PLAYER only
    (`v.startsWith('/') ? 'file://' + v : v`); keep the plain path for
    `processVideoBackground`, trimmers, muxers and upload.

## Key exports

Capability: `isBackgroundFilterAvailable`, `getSegmentationSupport`,
`useSegmentationSupport`, `isCompositeCaptureSupported`, `isOfflineBakeSupported`,
`shouldBakeBackground`
Surfaces: `VisionCameraSurface`, `ExpoCameraSurface` (subpath `/surfaces/expo-camera`),
types `CameraSurfaceHandle`, `CameraRecording`, `CameraSurfaceProps`
Live: `useBackgroundFilter`, `BackgroundRendererView`
Record/bake: `startCompositeCapture`, `processVideoBackground`
Backgrounds: `DEFAULT_BACKGROUNDS`, `BACKGROUND_NONE`, `findBackground`, `hasBackgrounds`,
`isBackgroundSelected`, `resolveBackgroundUri`
Errors: `BackgroundFilterError` (`code`: unsupported | decode-failed | encode-failed |
cancelled | io), `bakeFailureReason`, `BakeCancelledError`, `isBakeCancelled`,
`isCancelledBakeError`
Host: `configureBackgroundFilterHost`, `resolveBackgroundFilterHost`,
`useBackgroundFilterHost`, `resetBackgroundFilterHost`

## Subpath exports

- `.` — everything above. Needs only the required peers.
- `./adapters/expo` — `createExpoBackgroundFilterHost`. Needs `expo-file-system`.
- `./surfaces/expo-camera` — `ExpoCameraSurface`. Needs `expo-camera`.

Importing a subpath is what pulls its dependency into the bundle. Skip the subpath and
you do not need the dependency.

## Top failure modes

- `supported: false` on a capable device → native not linked → `prebuild --clean`, rebuild.
- Android autolinking misses it, iOS fine → `react-native.config.js` platform entries must
  stay EMPTY; paths there resolve relative to the package root and silently point nowhere.
- `PRIVATE format … not supported for ImageAnalysis` → use `pixelFormat: 'yuv'`, not
  `'native'`.
- iOS clip has no audio → record as `.mov` on iOS, not `.mp4`. AVCaptureMovieFileOutput
  always writes QuickTime; the mp4 parser then discards the audio track.
- Audio ~370 ms ahead → start the camera recorder FIRST and await it, then the capture.
- Filtered clip is a different shape than an unfiltered one → pass `aspectRatio` (e.g.
  `9/16`) to `startCompositeCapture`.
- Android `trying to draw too large bitmap` → background images must be near 1080x1920;
  the native downscale does not protect your own thumbnails.
- Capture never runs, always bakes → no `cacheDirectory` configured. Wire `onWarn` to see.
- Android video plays but the expo-video thumbnail strip is empty (iOS fine) → the uri is
  schemeless; prefix `file://` for the player only. See rule 11.
